items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: Anyway, Clyde Hart did a lot... He showed me a lot of things about playing the piano.

ctx.x: Anyway, I want to kind of backtrack and mention these people. And I think I mentioned Clyde Hart, when I was talking about the band that worked with us at the Yacht Club when I was there with Trummy Young. I mentioned Clyde Hart working with Coleman Hawkins and Dizzy Gillespie, Oscar Pettiford and Jackie Miles.

Anyway, Clyde Hart did a lot... He showed me a lot of things about playing the piano. Clyde was quite a busy musician then. He was making a lot of record dates and doing a lot of writing, and he was very much in demand. Unfortunately, he died not long after that. I think it was around this time when... I don't know whether it was at that particular time, or whether... I think it was probably later. Because a couple of years later, after I had worked in that Eckstine band, I did go back to 52nd Street, and I…
But the reason I'm saying this is that little incidents come to mind that happened. By this time, I had heard Bud Powell in New York, and had learned to respect him very much.
